questions.question: D1 — Add gstack skill routing rules to this project's CLAUDE.md? Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-bbDT0N on main, reviewing PLAN.md. ELI10: gstack works best when CLAUDE.md tells the agent which slash skill to reach for (bugs → /investigate, ship → /ship, etc). Without it you invoke skills by hand each time. Stakes if wrong: none permanent, it's a text block you can delete. Recommendation: A because it is a two-way door and saves manual routing. Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score. Net: convenience vs keeping a fixture CLAUDE.md untouched. (In plan mode, the edit and commit happen after plan approval.)

options.label: Add routing rules (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Future requests auto-route to the right gstack skill without typing slash names. ✅ Two-way door: a plain text section you can delete any time. ❌ Adds a section to a CLAUDE.md that is currently a review fixture and commits it.

options.label: No thanks, manual invocation
options.description: ✅ CLAUDE.md stays exactly as the fixture author wrote it, no extra commit. ✅ You keep full control over when a skill fires. ❌ Every skill has to be invoked by name each time; no proactive suggestions.

questions.question: D2 — Enable cross-project learnings search? Project/branch/task: same repo, plan-ceo-review preamble. ELI10: gstack can search learnings recorded from your other projects on this machine to spot patterns that apply here. Everything stays local. Good for solo devs; skip if you juggle multiple client codebases where cross-contamination matters. Stakes if wrong: a wrong choice just means noisier or sparser prior-learning hints; flip it any time with gstack-config. Recommendation: A because a single-developer machine gets more signal from pooled learnings. Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score. Net: more context vs strict per-project isolation.

options.label: Enable cross-project (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Reviews surface 'prior learning applied' hints from every project on this machine. ✅ Data never leaves the machine; only a local config flag changes. ❌ Learnings from unrelated client codebases could show up where they don't apply.

options.label: Project-scoped only
options.description: ✅ Zero risk of one client's patterns leaking into another client's review. ✅ Learnings stay tightly relevant to this repo. ❌ This repo has 0 learnings today, so prior-learning hints will be empty for a while.

questions.question:
D2 — Search learnings across your other projects on this machine?
Project/branch/task: same fixture; this project has zero learnings so far.
ELI10: gstack keeps notes on pitfalls and patterns it learns per project. Cross-project mode lets it also read notes from your other repos on this machine when reviewing this one. Everything stays local. Good for a solo developer; skip if you work on separate client codebases where cross-contamination matters.
Stakes if we pick wrong: low. Either you miss a relevant prior lesson, or a lesson from an unrelated codebase gets applied where it does not fit.
Recommendation: A because this project has no learnings of its own yet, so cross-project is the only way any prior lesson can help.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Net: broader recall vs strict per-project isolation.

options.label: Project-scoped only
